Home/Lesson plans

Two learning paths

Start where you are. Build towards independence.

Both paths are designed for hands-on delivery. The beginner path assumes no embedded-systems experience; the advanced path expects basic C syntax, simple circuit wiring, and confidence using the Arduino IDE.

Foundation

Beginner: first principles to connected prototype.

Ten lessons · suggested 20–30 guided hours · suitable for teens and adult beginners.

Embedded systems & safe lab practice

Recognise system inputs, processing, outputs, power paths, polarity, current limits, and safe wiring habits.

2 hours

Arduino IDE & your first C program

Install the ESP32 board support, select the target, compile, upload, and understand setup(), loop(), variables, and functions.

2–3 hours

Digital outputs: LED & RGB

Use pinMode(), digitalWrite(), delays, constants, and simple functions while measuring the output state.

2 hours

Digital inputs & decisions

Read buttons, use internal pull-ups, write if/else logic, debounce contacts, and build a responsive controller.

2–3 hours

Analogue sensing & PWM output

Read an analogue sensor, scale values, and control apparent LED brightness or another safe load with PWM.

3 hours

Serial monitor & evidence-led debugging

Print variables, check assumptions, recognise compiler versus runtime faults, and change one factor at a time.

2 hours

I²C sensors and displays

Understand SDA, SCL, addressing, scanning, library use, and presenting live information on an OLED or LCD.

3 hours

SPI peripherals & colour TFT

Wire clock and data lines, configure chip-select pins, run a display test, and diagnose blank-screen causes.

3 hours

Wi‑Fi & a local web control

Join a network, understand client/server roles, exchange simple data, and keep credentials out of shared code.

3 hours

Capstone: useful connected device

Plan, wire, code, test, demonstrate, and explain a device with an input, decision, output, and diagnostic method.

4–6 hours

System design

Advanced: responsive, connected, maintainable.

Ten lessons · suggested 30–40 guided hours · for learners who can already upload and modify a basic sketch.

Embedded C architecture

Use types, pointers, structs, const correctness, modular files, and clear hardware abstractions.

3 hours

Timing, state machines & responsiveness

Replace blocking delays with elapsed-time logic, formalise states, and reason about transition conditions.

3 hours

Interrupts, timers & shared data

Write short interrupt service routines, protect shared state, and choose when polling is the safer design.

3–4 hours

FreeRTOS tasks & coordination

Separate concurrent work, set task priorities thoughtfully, use queues or notifications, and avoid race conditions.

4 hours

Robust serial buses

Compare UART, I²C, SPI, and I²S; validate wiring and timing; recover from missing or invalid peripheral data.

3–4 hours

Displays, buffers & PSRAM

Manage graphics memory, confirm PSRAM configuration, reduce redraw work, and diagnose allocation failures.

3–4 hours

BLE provisioning & Wi‑Fi lifecycle

Model provisioning states, handle events safely, persist configuration, and make recovery behaviour visible.

4 hours

IoT device model & cloud control

Represent nodes, devices, and parameters; design callbacks; compare managed platforms with direct MQTT.

3–4 hours

Flash partitions, NVS, OTA & security

Select a partition layout, plan update and rollback behaviour, store settings, and apply credential hygiene.

4 hours

Capstone: dependable IoT product prototype

Write requirements, partition the design, instrument failures, test recovery, and communicate trade-offs in a review.

6–8 hours
A

Delivery format

Individual, small-group, workshop, or modular course. Online and in-person options are subject to arrangement.

B

Equipment

ESP32-S3 development board, data-capable USB cable, breadboard, basic components, and selected project modules.

C

Assessment

Short demonstrations, code explanation, fault-finding exercises, design journal, and a final working prototype.

Need a customised plan?

Lessons can be adapted for age, prior experience, class duration, available hardware, and a chosen capstone.
